walkthroughs.body_html:
Databases — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Databases brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Databases.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of database normalisation?
options: 11 (counting the 1s).
To make the database look neater.
To reduce redundancy and avoid update anomalies.
To make the database run faster.

mcqs.q: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: 11 (counting the 1s).
Only rows with matching values in both tables.
All rows from both tables combined.
Only the inner columns of each table.

mcqs.q: What is the denary value of binary 10110?
options: 11 (counting the 1s).
Only the inner columns of each table.
10110 (treating it as a denary number).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Entity”?
options: Constraint that every foreign key value must match an existing primary key in the referenced table.
Real-world object the database stores information about; modelled as a table.
Codd's 1970 model representing data as tables (relations) of tuples (rows).
Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability - properties of reliable transactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Join”?
options: Association between entities, classified as one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many.
Constraint that every foreign key value must match an existing primary key in the referenced table.
Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability - properties of reliable transactions.
SQL operation combining rows from two or more tables based on related columns.
